lee: Heads up — noticing ~15% drop in priming cache hit-rate on canary after the recent kernel relayout (matmul reorder + quant switch).
omar: which canary and model?
lee: canary=hosted-v2, model=redwood-open-7b-quant-a2, kernel_build=relayout-2026-03-12 (fused_reorder_v3). baseline before relayout hit ~72%, now ~57% across p95 traffic.
marta: any change in tokenizer or input normalization?
lee: tokenizer config unchanged. Quick profiling shows increased first-token latency and KV lookup p95 spikes.
lee: Logs snapshot:
```
KVLookup(ms) p50=0.8 p95=4.2 prev_p95=1.1
PrimingHitRate=0.57 (was 0.72)
kernel_variant=fused_reorder_v3
```
ci-bot: deploy canary completed for relayout-2026-03-12 (build 1337) :white_check_mark:
omar: sounds like a keying issue rather than eviction. @dana can you pull KV key fingerprints from traces?
dana: grabbing traces now. quick grep shows key size distribution is identical but ~60% of keys differ byte-wise at offsets 8-11 between v2 and v3 runs.
dana: hypothesis: internal padding/memlayout change in the fused matmul path is mutating the buffer used to compute the key.
lee: repro locally with a tiny harness. see below:
```
# run
python tools/kv_hash_check.py --model redwood-open-7b --kernel fused_reorder_v2
# output: key=0x9a12b7f3...
# run with fused_reorder_v3 -> key=0x9b34c8d2...
```
marta: is this limited to quantized kernels?
lee: looks correlated. floating point (fp16) path shows stable keys. quant int8 path applies block padding and a memcpy reorder, which seems to leak into the hash input.
odar: (typo, ignore)
omar: mitigation options?
dana: short term: add a normalization layer before hashing that strips transient padding bytes or masks canonical padding fields so hashes are stable across kernel layouts. Long term: fix kernel to preserve deterministic bytes for KV key inputs or expose a stable keying API.
lee: rolled a hotfix to canary that normalizes the key (strip/zero out padding region) — priming_hit_rate back up to ~0.69 within 30m. pushing to staging for broader validation.
metrics-bot: priming_hit_rate hosted-v2/canary: 2026-03-15T14:12 -> 0.57, 2026-03-15T15:10 -> 0.69 after key-normalization patch.
marta: good short-term. Please add a regression test that fuzzes kernel variants and validates key invariants. Also include a perf check: normalization must not add >1% p50 latency.
lee: will open PR with tests + perf note. tagging infra: @infra-team — need scheduled perf baselines across quant profiles (int8, int4) before promoting.
omar: also consider a canary policy that gates kernel relayouts on priming_hit_rate delta < 3% to catch these earlier.
dana: filing kernel bug with repro and trace dump.
lee: filed issue: github.com/redwood/runtime/issues/5478 — includes repro, traces, and the hotfix branch.
marta: nice work. once kernel fix lands we can remove the normalization hotfix but keep the test in place.
lee: TL;DR: kernel relayout changed intermediate memory layout used by quant path, mutated bytes that feed KV key computation, causing large priming cache hit-rate drop. Hotfix normalizes keys; permanent fix needs kernel change.
omar: thanks everyone — continuing monitoring. :eyes:
